title: Garlic and Coriander Butter Naan
summary: Yoghurt naan dough is studded with garlic, charred in a very hot pan and brushed generously with warm garlic ghee and chopped coriander.
equipment: heavy cast-iron frying pan or tawa

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Combine the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and baking powder in a large bowl, then work in the yoghurt, water and 2 tbsp melted ghee until a soft, tacky dough forms. Knead for 5 minutes until it feels smooth.

steps.title: Prove
steps.text: Cover the bowl and leave in a warm spot for 1.5-2 hours, until the dough has doubled.

steps.title: Form
steps.text: Divide into 8, roll each into a ball and let them relax for 10 minutes, then stretch or roll each one into a 22 cm teardrop, 5 mm thick.

steps.title: Make the garlic butter
steps.text: Warm the ghee and garlic over low heat for 2 minutes until fragrant but not browned. Take off the heat and stir in most of the coriander.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Heat the frying pan over high heat for 3 minutes. Brush the top of a naan with water, press a little of the garlic into the dry side and lay it wet side down. Cook 1-1.5 minutes until bubbled and charred underneath.

steps.title: Char
steps.text: Flip and cook 1 minute more until the garlic side is golden and spotted.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Brush with garlic butter, scatter with the remaining coriander and wrap in a tea towel while you cook the rest. Serve hot.

tips: Keep the garlic butter on low heat; browned garlic tastes bitter.
Press the garlic firmly into the dough so it stays put when you flip.
Chop the coriander finely so it clings to the butter.
storage: Keep wrapped at room temperature and eat within 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Refresh in a hot oven for a few minutes. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
